body: Development includes changes in the structure and function of the body over time. Early in development, repeated cell division produces groups of cells. Cells differentiate as they take on distinct roles, such as contributing to muscle or nervous tissue.

Inherited variants help shape biological development together with conditions before and after birth. During growth and aging, bodies change at different rates. For example, inherited differences and lived conditions can contribute to differences in mobility in later life.

limitations: A life-stage sequence is a simplified description of development. It cannot predict an individual's health, milestones or experience.
purpose: Connect human development to inheritance, regulation and environment.
